source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 October 1937, p. 5 ("Cookstown, October 9 1937" notes column)
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: image-read (BNA page 5 crop, column 1): 'Messrs. W. H. Newell, William Gough, James Wright and Samuel Cowan, the four retiring members of Cookstown Urban Council, were the only persons nominated on Tuesday for the four vacancies. They were, therefore, declared elected by Mr. J. W. Fleming, Returning Officer.' (BNA search lists the item as p. 4; the article image is page 5.)

note: Annual retirement of one third (four seats), the ordinary day having been moved from 15 May to 15 October 1937. Nominations were taken on Tuesday 5 October 1937; the four retiring members were the only persons nominated and were declared elected by the Returning Officer, Mr. J. W. Fleming (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 October 1937, p. 5). They are the third elected in January 1934 (Balmer, Wright, Newell, Gough), with Samuel Cowan in place of Robert E. Balmer. Returned unopposed. Samuel Cowan is described as a retiring member, so he had presumably been co-opted in the term in place of Robert E. Balmer (elected January 1934); the co-option is not found. The annual meeting of the council (Mid-Ulster Mail, 30 October 1937, p. 3) lists Newell, Gough and Wright among the members present; Cowan is not in that list.
